newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nanjing Post to offer 100 mln B shares this month.
newsitem.headline: Nanjing Post to offer 100 mln B shares this month.

text.p: Nanjing Post and Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd will launch an initial public offering of 100 million B shares by the end of this month, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

The offer will carry a P/E (price/earnings) ratio of between eight and nine times based on net profits of about 51 million yuan, or 0.24 yuan per share, estimated for 1996 under international accounting standards, the spokesman said.
The B shares will be listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Nanjing Post has appointed China Southern Securities as the domestic lead underwriter and Hoare Govett (Asia) Ltd the global coordinator, the official said.
Nanjing Post will use the share proceeds to develop a new line producing telecommunications equipment and to finance technological upgrades, he said.
The company, based in Nanjing, capital of eastern China's Jiangsu province, had unaudited net profits of 26 million yuan in 1995 and 16 million the previous year.
The company has 115 million outstanding state shares, owned by the China Post and Telecommunications Industry Corp, the official said.
Classified as a high-tech enterprise, Nanjing Post is entitled to a favourable tax rate, he said, but did not issue a profit forecast or provide details.
Nanjing Post is among the 33 firms that have been approved by the Securities Commission of the State Council, China's cabinet, to list foreign currency B shares.
